reason: A read fan-out CAN still fork — on the ANSWER rather than on state (that is exactly what compute_reverse_batch did). Its docstring claims the bulk reprojection is byte-identical to the per-block read_block path including the dense `position` rank, and that claim is already falsifiable: reads.rs::read_blocks_bulk_tests projects every block BOTH ways and compares, on a flat 200-sibling space and on a scrambled multi-parent one (nested_multi_parent_bulk_positions_match_per_block). Widening the scan is what made this coverage visible to the ratchet

ONE BODY: a single-expression delegate to import_payload_with_changed_purged_tagscope(ImportPayload::Batch(..)), the same body the single-blob path reaches with ImportPayload::Single. Everything after the doc.import* call — diff capture, no-op short-circuit, legacy-migration fallback, changed/purged/tag-scope resolution — is payload-agnostic and shared. The batch-vs-single difference lives inside loro's own import_batch (one detached append per blob, one re-attach), not in this crate

N-key SELECT fan-out; no writes. NOTE it carries an internal equivalence claim of its own — a positional IN(?,?,..) branch under SMALL_IN_LIMIT and a json_each(?) branch above it, documented as returning identical row sets. That is a batch-vs-batch parity, not a batch-vs-single one, and it forks nothing durable: a divergence would surface as a wrong read, never as divergent state

N-key space-resolution fan-out (one chunked SELECT replacing resolve_block_space's N+1); appends no op_log rows and mutates nothing. Its soft-delete filtering is documented to match resolve_block_space exactly, and add_tags_by_ids_inner's `converged` note already leans on it being a read-only pre-check

Not a fan-out at all: a two-line upper-bound check on a length, shared by the *_by_ids / batch family so they all reject an over-cap batch with one verbatim message. Caught by the name heuristic (`batch` segment), kept in the inventory rather than regex-excluded — narrowing the heuristic is how a real fan-out escapes it

A GENUINE, UNCOVERED FORK — the one the widened scan was worth doing for. It collapses N imports + N projections + N slot deletes into one LoroDoc::import_batch, one union projection and one tx, against a per-slot sibling (replay_inbox_row) it also FALLS BACK to on any batch error. The fallback is the tell: the code already assumes the two arms are interchangeable. Their inputs differ in ways an oracle should pin — the batch gates blobs against a CUMULATIVE version base (gate_replay_blobs) where the per-row path gates each alone, and it purges the UNION of the batch's tombstones. No oracle yet: the harness in src-tauri/src/bulk_equivalence/ is app-crate, #[cfg(test)], and drives SQL+op_log state, while this arm's observable surface is a LoroDoc, the loro_sync_inbox/quarantine tables and a BatchReplayOutcome in another crate — a real scenario needs a sync-side harness, not a scenario file. Recorded as owed work rather than argued away; #3346 follow-up

A PARTITIONER, not a fan-out: it slices one Vec<OpTransfer> into size-bounded chunks so each fits LORO_INLINE_MAX_BYTES on the wire. Pure, no I/O, no single-item sibling to agree with — the thing that must agree with a fold is its CALLER's ingest, not the slicing

ALREADY A FOLD: it loops the records and calls insert_replicated_op — the single-record ingest entry point — once each. There is one write body. What the loop adds around it is policy, not a second implementation (per-device stall/defer, #3726 ascending-seq reporting, #3727 stall accounting). CAVEAT on the `kind` field: this WRITES, but computes `read-only`, because insert_replicated_op's write is one more hop away in another crate (agaric_engine::dag::ingest_replicated_record) and the discriminator expands exactly one level and does not cross files. Recorded here rather than papered over: the recorded kind is the computed kind, and this reason is what the kind does not say
